jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Reveal
jokes.joke: My dietician told me to stop thinking of meals as entertainment. That’s difficult because I eat like I’m producing a Vegas stage show: appetizers enter through smoke, the entrée gets a spotlight, and dessert descends from the ceiling. She asked, “Where do vegetables fit in?” I said, “They’re backstage. Nobody paid to see them.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Cheat Day Forever
jokes.joke: I fired my dietician. Not because the diet failed — because I found out she went home and told her husband about my cheat days. Like it was gossip. Ma'am, I trusted you with my macros and my dignity, and you sold me out for dinner conversation. I've forgiven exes, forgiven my dad, forgiven a guy who backed into my car and drove off. But her? Never. I will hold this grudge with the same discipline I never once held a diet.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Fuel Source
jokes.joke: My dietician told me I need to learn to forgive people, because carrying around all that toxic resentment is like swallowing poison. I told her, 'Look, you put me on a six-hundred-calorie deficit. That resentment is currently my only source of energy. If I let go of what my brother-in-law said at Thanksgiving four years ago, my organs will shut down.'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Humorless Dietician
jokes.joke: I have the most humorless dietician in the world. Last appointment I said, 'I cheated on my diet with a donut.' She didn't even crack a smile. Just looked at me and said, 'That's not a cheat. That's a full-blown affair. And the scale is going to find out.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Nutritional Grudge
jokes.joke: My dietician told me, "You don't have a weight problem, you have a portion-control problem." That was three years ago, and I've lost thirty pounds just so I can run into her and say, "Interesting diagnosis, doctor." At this point my biggest calorie source is the grudge I'm still carrying around.

scores.comment: Strong escalation and a clean closing callback; the premise is relatable, though the betrayal setup is somewhat manufactured.
Clear premise, efficient escalation, and the resentment-as-calories turn lands sharply; strongest final line in the batch.
Readable and stage-friendly, but the diet-as-affair metaphor is familiar and the punchline follows the setup too predictably.
Good structure and a coherent grudge payoff, but the final calorie/grudge line is more clever than laugh-heavy and partly restates the premise.
Clean escalating Vegas-production conceit with a sharp, earned closing line.
Solid premise but the 'organs shut down' close is a bit flat and predictable.
Nice irony that the 'humorless' dietician delivers the funniest line; tight and natural.
Good callback structure but similar grudge-as-fuel idea lands softer than its sibling joke.
Fun theatrical escalation with a clean stage premise, though the vegetables backstage punchline is slightly predictable.
Strong stand-up cadence and escalation. The final line snaps the premise shut cleanly with good rhythm and character voice.
Undermines its own premise: the dietician's retort is actually an intentional witty quip rather than humorless, and the punchline feels like a stock quote.
Solid spite-motivation premise, but losing weight out of pettiness feels slightly muddled against a 'portion-control' diagnosis, softening the final snap.
Clean meal-as-production image with a solid closer, but the laugh stays mild.
Good trust-betrayal setup that lands the discipline inversion cleanly.
Tight link of calorie deficit to held resentment with a sharp final escalation.
Competent grudge-revenge angle but the turn and closer stay soft.
Clear premise and imagery; backstage vegetables is a decent payoff but fairly predictable.
Strong grudge escalation and clean callback tying discipline to dieting; solid stand-up structure.
Resentment-as-fuel angle is fresh, escalates well, and lands on a strong absurd image.
Readable and concise, but the affair metaphor is familiar and the biggest laugh comes from the dietician, not the comic.
